title: Schedule a cron job that writes a log and never runs twice at once
summary: A cron job runs a command at fixed times. Wrapping it in flock stops a new run from starting while the previous one still holds the lock, and sending its output to a log file lets you check what happened.

steps.explain: Create the folder for the log file.

placeholders.name: LOG_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the job's log file

steps.explain: Run the job once by hand through the same lock and log that cron will use. The exit code 0 means the job worked.
steps.expect: The line 'job exit code: 0' and the job's output in nightly.log.

placeholders.name: LOCK_FILE
placeholders.description: Lock file that stops a second run

placeholders.name: JOB_SCRIPT
placeholders.description: Absolute path to the job script or program

placeholders.name: LOG_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the job's log file

steps.explain: Add one line to your crontab: run the job every day at 02:30. The existing lines are kept, because the current list is read first. In a crontab line a percent sign must be written as \%.

placeholders.name: LOCK_FILE
placeholders.description: Lock file that stops a second run

placeholders.name: JOB_SCRIPT
placeholders.description: Absolute path to the job script or program

placeholders.name: LOG_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the job's log file

steps.explain: Check that the line was saved once.
steps.expect: The line that starts with '30 2 * * *' and contains flock and the job path.

steps.explain: After the scheduled time, read the end of the log. Cron does not show errors on screen, so the log is the only report.
steps.expect: Output from the last run. A missing file means cron has not run the job yet.

placeholders.name: LOG_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the job's log file

rollback.explain: Remove the job's line from the crontab and keep all other lines.

placeholders.name: JOB_SCRIPT
placeholders.description: Path that appears in the line to remove

warnings: Writing 'crontab -' replaces the whole crontab. The command in step 3 keeps the existing lines, so check 'crontab -l' afterwards.
Cron runs with a short PATH and no login shell. Use absolute paths for every program and script in the line.
flock -n skips the run and exits with code 1 when the previous run still holds the lock. That is the intended behaviour.
